messages:
Anna (platform): Quick heads-up — after the v2 rollout some tenants are still charged against the v2 quota even though requests are landing on v1 for output. Noticed via billing diff on a customer call this AM. Anyone else see quota attribution mismatch?
Mike (infra): I saw a small spike in route-affinity drift last night. Looks like fallback logic is picking v1 for routing, but quota attribution uses the auth-token -> default-route map which wasn’t updated.
Sachin (api): Hmm — that matches an edge we introduced when we made implicit-version fallthrough opt-in. Current pseudocode:
```
if headers.get("X-Route-Version"):
  route = headers["X-Route-Version"]
elif headers.get("X-Client-Version") == "1":
  route = "v1"
else:
  route = "v2"
# quota attribution uses token->route in DB (old mapping)
```
Mike (infra): Exactly. So requests end up on v1 but the billing pipeline sees token->v2 which was the last explicit assignment.
Jess (console): From UX side, customers are confused because our console shows "Requests: v1" but "Quota pool: v2" in the usage card for the tenant. Not great. We should add a small badge explaining "routing fallthrough" and surface the effective route used for quota evaluation.
Lucas (sre): Can we add a metric to bridge the two signals? Something like `route_effective{tenant,route}` and `quota_assigned{tenant,route}` and an alert when they diverge > 1% for 1h. I can own the alert.
Sachin (api): I can change the attribution logic to compute quota route from the same resolved `route` used by the router at request time. Minimal change: persist `resolved_route` in the request envelope before handing off to billing.
Anna (platform): That sounds right — do we worry about retroactive billing for requests already processed? We should avoid replaying historical data.
Sachin (api): No retro billing — just future requests. For existing mismatches we'll create a telemetry query and a dashboard row to show the divergence.
Jess (console): Dashboard query suggestion for Console (PromQL):
```
sum by (tenant,route) (increase(api_requests_total{job="router"}[1h])) as requests
sum by (tenant,route) (increase(billing_events_total[1h])) as billed
# then compute requests/billed per tenant
```
Mike (infra): Also: client libs are still sending `X-Client-Version` inconsistently. Could we deprecate implicit `X-Client-Version` -> route mapping in the next minor and instead require `X-Route-Version` or a console per-tenant override?
Anna (platform): We want a smooth deprecation path. Proposal: 1) Emit deprecation banner in console for tenants with fallback enabled; 2) Start a 90-day opt-in window where fallthrough is logged as a warning; 3) After 90 days, fallback disabled by default for new tenants. Thoughts?
Lucas (sre): +1 on banner + alert. I'll add an SLO guard so we don't auto-disable fallbacks for tenants with active incidents.
Jess (console): I'll add a small UX: Toggle "Enable legacy fallthrough" and a link to a one-click migrate that sets explicit route in tenant settings. Also surface the last 7-day divergence metric on the tenant usage page.
Sachin (api): I'll land the `resolved_route` header persist in the envelope and add a tiny e2e test. Planning to patch the billing writer to prefer envelope.resolved_route when present.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment v2.1 -> router-service completed: canary=5% -> status=ok :white_check_mark:
Anna (platform): OK, action items: Sachin patch + e2e, Jess console banner + dashboard row, Lucas alert and SLO guard, Mike to audit client libs that still send only X-Client-Version. I'll sync with Sales on the tenant call to explain no retro billing. Thanks. :thumbsup:
